primary_activity: A single resident performs focused computer and paperwork sessions at a daylight-oriented workstation.
secondary_activities: Read long-form material away from the screen
Retrieve active files and reference books
Hold a brief one-person conversation beside the work area
circulation_plan: Entry is through the west side of the south wall. A clear diagonal route runs northeast from the inward door clearance to the desk chair, then branches east toward a compact reading seat; the central-south floor remains free for turning and moving between both zones.
spatial_organization: The workstation occupies the north daylight band without centering the entire room on a wall-facing desk. Tall reference storage is consolidated on the west wall beyond the door swing, while a small reading cluster uses the quieter east side.
daylight_or_opening_considerations: A wide north window lights the desk from the side/front without being blocked by tall storage. The south door clearance and its northeast continuation remain furniture-free.
intended_furniture_groups: desk, task chair, and low drawer cabinet as the active work group
lounge chair and side table as a separate reading group
bookcase and file cabinet as a west-wall reference group
intended_open_space: An irregular open wedge from the south-west entry through the room center, plus pull-back clearance behind the task chair and approach space in front of west-wall storage.
difference_from_previous_scenes: Conceived before inspecting prior coordinates: this room uses a north-side daylight workstation, vertically consolidated west-wall storage, and an independent east reading pocket connected by diagonal rather than axial circulation.
